summary: Intermittent high p99 and 504s from failover to remote mirrored variant causing image-pull cold-starts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightGuide reported intermittent user-facing 504s and p99 latency spikes (~8–12s) for text-generation routes over a 3-hour window. Impact: degraded UX for chat flows and increased token retries; revenue-impacting for high-volume workflows.

Impact:
- ~2.5% of requests returned 504 during the peak window (15:20–18:40 PDT 2026-03-10).
- p50 stayed ~90–150ms; p95 ~350–600ms; p99 spiked to 8–12s.
- Errors correlated with sustained traffic surge from BrightGuide and some other dedicated tenants.

Environment:
- Customer on Dedicated pool (dedicated-us-west-1); routing policy includes overflow to a remote mirrored standby in us-east for capacity smoothing.
- Serving runtime: 2026.02.1 build; autoscaler policy: burst_enabled=true, overflow_target=remote_mirror.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Send sustained generation traffic with ~50 concurrent sessions targeting open-mpt-7b-instruct pinned to latest.
2) At autoscaler saturation, routing layer routes a fraction of overflow traffic to the configured remote mirror variant in us-east.
3) Several requests routed to new replicas in the mirror started exhibiting long cold image pulls (6–10s) before containers became ready; requests timed out at client 5s or returned 504 from gateway.

Observed logs / metrics / evidence:
- Gateway traces (trace IDs attached in comments) show socket established -> upstream connect delay ~6500–9800ms -> 504.
- Kube events on mirror cluster show repeated "Pulling" -> "BackOff" for image redwood/serving-runtime:2026-02.1 followed by successful pull. Image registry returned 429/502 intermittently during window.
- Container registry metrics show a short-lived rate limit spike for pulls from us-east cluster between 15:15–18:50 PDT (rate-limiter triggered due to shared mirror image pulls).
- Routing decision logs show overflow policy metrics: 12% of customer requests were overflowed to mirror during the peak.

Investigation notes (timeline):
- 2026-03-10 15:30 Support received alert from BrightGuide via /support channel reporting slow chats and retries.
- 15:40 L1 triage confirmed elevated 504s; opened this ticket and paged SRE.
- 16:05 SRE inspected cluster events and saw image pull BackOffs in the mirror cluster; correlated with registry 429s.
- 16:30 Eng verified routing config change made earlier that morning (PR merged 2026-03-10 08:12) introduced a temporary overflow-to-mirror threshold lowering to 60% when CPU saturation > 70%. That policy caused more traffic to be diverted during the surge.
- 17:00 Support applied a mitigation (disabled overflow-to-remote-mirror for affected customers) which immediately reduced cross-region pulls and 504s.

Root cause:
A routing-policy change reduced the overflow threshold, triggering follow-the-load routing to a remote mirror pool in us-east. The mirror pool had recently been scaled down and relied on on-demand container pulls from the central registry; during the traffic surge multiple replicas attempted image pulls and hit registry rate limits (429/502), leading to image-pull cold-start delays. These delayed readiness led to request timeouts / 504s. The combined effect of policy change + scaled-down mirror + transient registry throttling produced the observed p99 spikes.

Immediate mitigation and resolution:
- at 17:00, Support and SRE disabled overflow-to-remote-mirror for affected customers and reverted the threshold to pre-2026-03-10 values.
- SRE temporarily increased min_replicas for mirror pool and warmed images by pre-pulling the serving-runtime image to mirror nodes.
- Eng reverted the policy change via PR #998 and scheduled controlled rollout for a guarded config release.

Follow-up actions (postmortem items):
- Mirror pool image pre-warm: add automated pre-pull during scale events (action: infra, ETA 2 weeks).
- Routing policy guardrails: add an integration test that simulates registry throttling and ensures overflow does not route >5% to remote mirrors in first 10 minutes of surge (action: routing team, ETA 1 week).
- Registry hardening: coordinate with registry provider to request higher pull quota for mirror cluster and add cached image artifact in us-east (action: infra ops, ETA 1 week).
- Customer communication: sent incident summary and credits to BrightGuide for incident window.

Status: Resolved — mitigations applied and changes reverted. Monitoring in place to catch regressions.

2026-03-10 17:05 — Javier Morales (Assignee): 'Applied temporary rollback of overflow policy and pre-pulled images to mirror nodes. Observed 504s drop to baseline within 5 minutes. Will follow up with code rollback and runbook updates.'

resolution: Rollback of routing threshold and temporary disable of remote overflow; increased min_replicas and pre-pulled images to mirror nodes; reverted policy change (PR merged revert). Follow-up tasks scheduled as infra and routing backlog items. Incident credited to customer as goodwill.
